processes.title: Omnichannel Sales Promotions
processes.memory_hook: Pricing asks an external promotion brain.
processes.business_intent: Enrich sales-order pricing with promotion logic evaluated by SAP Omnichannel Promotion Pricing using sales-order context and optional additional attributes.

control_plane.why: add business context not covered by fixed fields
keeps promotion evaluation outside the core order transaction

data_hinges.changes: pricing outcome in the sales order

impact_summary: Adds a side-by-side pricing decision without turning promotion management into a new sales-order type.
constraints: It is an overlay, not a substitute for core pricing governance.
Additional attributes require coordinated configuration on both sides of the integration.
lead_questions: Who owns the promotion truth: ERP pricing or promotion service?
What happens if the service is unavailable?
Which attributes must be auditable for a disputed promotion?

processes.title: Related Objects & Process Flow
processes.memory_hook: A sales document is a node in a chain, not an isolated record.
processes.business_intent: Expose business relationships around a sales document so users and integrations can navigate preceding, subsequent, and related objects.

control_plane.why: make relationships consumable by external tools
determines how reference relationships are created

data_hinges.changes: what external or adjacent context is discoverable
diagnostic view of where execution stopped

impact_summary: Improves diagnosis, audit and AI grounding because a question can traverse the transaction chain rather than search isolated documents.
constraints: A related object is not automatically the cause of a downstream outcome.
Custom relationships need clear ownership and lifecycle rules.
lead_questions: What is the predecessor that supplied this value?
Can an AI answer cite the actual lineage rather than infer it from timestamps?
